sourcesContent: import React from "react"; import { Container, Typography, Box, Paper, Button, Alert, } from "@mui/material"; import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"; import { ArrowBack, Warning } from "@mui/icons-material"; import Navigation from "../../components/Navigation"; const Top5MistakesPage: React.FC = () => { const navigate = useNavigate(); const mistakes = [ { title: "1. Choosing the Lowest Premium Without Checking Coverage", problem: "Many people select insurance based solely on the lowest monthly premium, ignoring what the plan actually covers.", consequence: "You might end up with high out-of-pocket costs when you need care, or discover critical services aren't covered.", solution: "Compare total potential costs including deductibles, co-pays, and out-of-pocket maximums. A slightly higher premium might save you thousands in the long run.", }, { title: "2. Not Disclosing Pre-existing Conditions", problem: "Failing to disclose existing health conditions or medical history when purchasing insurance.", consequence: "Claims can be rejected, and your policy may be cancelled. Insurance fraud can have legal consequences.", solution: "Always provide complete and honest information about your health. Many insurers now cover pre-existing conditions after a waiting period.", }, { title: "3. Ignoring the Network of Hospitals", problem: "Not checking if your preferred hospitals and doctors are in the insurer's network.", consequence: "You may face significantly higher costs or have to switch healthcare providers. Emergency situations could lead to unexpected bills.", solution: "Verify your preferred hospitals are in-network. Check if there are quality network hospitals near your home and workplace.", }, { title: "4. Underestimating Coverage Amount", problem: "Choosing insufficient sum insured based on current healthcare costs without considering medical inflation.", consequence: "Medical costs are rising 10-15% annually. A ₹3 lakh cover today may not be adequate for a major illness in a few years.", solution: "Choose at least ₹5-10 lakh coverage. Consider your age, lifestyle, family history, and city's healthcare costs. Top-up plans can increase coverage affordably.", }, { title: "5. Not Reading the Policy Document", problem: "Relying only on the sales person's verbal promises without reading the actual policy terms and conditions.", consequence: "Surprises during claim settlement - discovering exclusions, waiting periods, sub-limits, or conditions you weren't aware of.", solution: "Read the policy document carefully, especially sections on exclusions, claim procedures, and renewal terms. Ask questions about anything unclear.", }, ]; return ( Top 5 Mistakes to Avoid Learn about common pitfalls when purchasing health insurance and how to avoid them. Did you know? According to industry data, over 30% of insurance claims face delays or rejections due to mistakes that could have been easily avoided during the purchase process. {mistakes.map((mistake, index) => ( {mistake.title} ❌ The Problem: {mistake.problem} ⚠️ The Consequence: {mistake.consequence} ✅ The Solution: {mistake.solution} ))} 💡 Make an Informed Decision Our AI-powered tool helps you avoid these mistakes by analyzing your needs and recommending the most suitable plans with transparent information. ); }; export default Top5MistakesPage;
